mechanism_narrative: An increase in the Federal Funds Rate by more than 0.5% within a month signals a tightening monetary policy, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as borrowing costs rise and economic activity slows.
failure_condition: If the 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 40% of the instances where FEDFUNDS increased by more than 0.5% within a month.

mechanism_narrative: A significant drop in housing starts (HOUST) by more than 5% in two months indicates a weakening demand in the housing market, which is a leading indicator of broader economic slowdown and thus negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If the 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of the instances where HOUST dropped by more than 5% within two months.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) by more than 0.5% in one month signals labor market weakness, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as it indicates a slowing economy.
failure_condition: If the 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of the instances where UNRATE increased by more than 0.5% within a month.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in industrial production (INDPRO) by more than 1% in two months signals a strengthening supply side of the economy, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as it indicates increased economic activity.
failure_condition: If the 60-day forward returns are negative in more than 40% of the instances where INDPRO increased by more than 1% within two months.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained low inflation environment, indicated by CPIAUCSL remaining below 2% for three consecutive months, suggests a stable economic environment conducive to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 50% of the instances where CPIAUCSL remained below 2% for three consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: When real personal consumption expenditures (RSAFS) grow by more than 1% month-over-month, it indicates strong consumer demand, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days as markets react to the positive economic signal.
failure_condition: If the 5-day forward returns are negative in more than 60% of the instances where RSAFS increased by more than 1% month-over-month.

mechanism_narrative: An interaction between a rising unemployment rate (UNRATE) and a decline in nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) by more than 0.5% month-over-month signals a weakening labor market, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of the instances where both UNRATE rose and PAYEMS dropped by more than 0.5% month-over-month.

mechanism_narrative: An interaction between a decline in GDP (GDPC1) and a rise in the Consumer Price Index (CPIAUCSL) by more than 0.5% month-over-month indicates stagflationary pressures, which typically lead to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If the 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of the instances where GDPC1 dropped and CPIAUCSL rose by more than 0.5% month-over-month.
